user.title: Connect to the WattMosaic engine
user.description:
Enter the address of the WattMosaic engine. The engine performs all inference and learning; this integration only reads its results.

Stored API token: {token_status}.

data_description.api_token: Sent as the X-API-Token header. Leave empty if the engine has no token configured.

hassio_confirm.title: WattMosaic App found

settings.title: Polling and freshness
settings.description: How often the integration polls the engine, and when data is considered stale or unavailable. The engine currently reports {channel_count} CT channel(s).

data_description.stale_after: Results older than this are not published as current measurements. Default 120 s.
data_description.unavailable_after: The engine is treated as offline after this long without a successful poll. Default 120 s.

channels.title: CT channel assignment

data_description.role: main = utility feed, branch = circuit, dedicated_device = single device.
data_description.paired_ct_id: The other leg of a double-pole load, if any.
data_description.device_id: Required for a dedicated_device CT. Suggestions are never applied automatically.

mapping.title: Device mapping
mapping.description:
Map {channel_name} ({channel_id}) to a device.

Suggested candidates ({candidate_count}):
{candidates}

Suggestions are never applied automatically. Pick a candidate, type a device ID, or skip.

confirm.title: Confirm topology

data_description.confirm_uncertain: Marks the topology confirmed in the engine. Leave unticked to keep it candidate, which is the normal choice when some rows are still assumptions.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure WattMosaic
reconfigure.description:
Update the engine connection. Leave the token empty to keep the current one.

Stored API token: {token_status}.

data_description.api_token: Leave empty to keep the stored token. The current token is never shown.

init.title: WattMosaic options
init.description:
Adjust polling and freshness thresholds. The engine currently reports {channel_count} CT channel(s).

Tick "Configure one device" to state what the engine cannot infer by itself (device type, monitoring, expected watts).

device_config.title: Configure a device
device_config.description:
Choose the device to describe. The engine reports {device_count} device(s): {device_ids}.

Pick one from the list or type its device id. One device is configured per visit; nothing else in the topology changes.

data_description.device_id: Devices the engine already knows about.
data_description.custom_device_id: Type an id to configure a device the engine did not list.

device_config_details.title: Device configuration
device_config_details.description:
Describe device {device_id}. Every field is optional knowledge: a blank value means "not stated", never zero watts.

State entities are comma-separated entity ids that prove the device is running. Mode entities are context only and never count as proof of load.

CT channels name the circuit this device sits on. Select several when other loads share the same circuit: the engine then reports the row as inferred and never pretends the CT measured this device alone.

Device link shows this load's power and energy under an existing Home Assistant device instead of a WattMosaic one. {link_count} device(s) can be linked from the entities this device already declares.

data.monitored_by_ct_ids: CT channels that meter this device
data.watts_per_bulb_on: Watts per bulb at full output (W)

data_description.connectivity: connected = HA holds an entity for it; not_connected = non-smart device.
data_description.monitoring: dedicated = its own CT; shared = a circuit with other loads; home_total_only = only visible in the total; unmonitored = no CT at all.
data_description.monitored_by_ct_ids: The CT rows that carry this load. Choose more than one only when they really are separate rows; several loads on one row is the shared-circuit case, settled by the switch states.
data_description.behavior: fixed = constant watts; variable = follows a dimmer/speed; complex = multi-state controller.
data_description.bulb_count: A five-bulb fixture at 9 W per bulb is 45 W, not 9 W.
data_description.controller_mode_entity_id: Context only: it never proves the appliance draws power.
data_description.controller_load_entity_ids: Entities that do prove runtime when active.
data_description.create_energy_sensor: Adds a total-increasing energy sensor for this load, attached to the linked device (or to the device its state entity belongs to when no link is chosen). Turn this off for loads you do not want in the Energy Dashboard.
data_description.ha_device_id: The device whose page should show this load's power and energy. Choose the top entry to keep the measurement on its own WattMosaic device. Only devices that own one of the declared state entities are offered.
